title: Pseudospin Hall Transport Induced by Berry Curvature
authors: Qinhui Jiang, Jidong Song, Qingyang Mo, Bo Li, Dongyi Wang, Shuang Zhang, Mengyao Li
abstract: Pseudospin-1 Dirac systems exhibit unique physics distinct from conventional Dirac cones, such as flat-band crossings and non-Abelian characteristics, yet their topological transport properties have remained largely untapped in passive, time-reversal-invariant settings. Here we uncover an in-plane polarity of the Berry-curvature texture in a pseudospin-1 Dirac Hamiltonian, a previously unexplored geometric degree of freedom encoded in the sign-resolved distribution of Berry curvature despite zero net Berry flux, and reveal a new mechanics where Berry curvature induce pseudospin Hall behaviors in a system. We show that the oriented coupling between this momentum-space polarity and a real-space mass gradient governs a geometric selection rule that dictates the emergence of gapless pseudospin Hall modes. By engineering the intracell couplings of a four-site planar lattice, we independently program the Berry-curvature polarity and the spatial mass gradient without altering the host lattice symmetry. Acoustic experiments directly confirm this directional selection rule: reversing the mass gradient closes or reopens the dispersive gap, while pseudospin-selective source excitation launches counterpropagating pseudospin branches along arbitrary prescribed axes. Our work establishes quantum geometric polarity as a versatile tool for reconfigurable wave routing, sensing, and high-capacity quantum applications.
summary: This paper introduces a novel mechanism where the topological properties of pseudospin-1 Dirac systems govern transport via a geometric matching condition between the Berry-curvature polarity and a real-space mass gradient. By engineering these two components independently in an acoustic lattice, the authors demonstrate the creation of robust, gapless pseudospin Hall waveguiding paths. This work establishes quantum geometric polarity as a versatile tool for reconfigurable wave routing.
main_problem: The research aims to utilize the topological transport properties of pseudospin-1 Dirac systems in passive, time-reversal-invariant settings to induce and control pseudospin Hall behaviors.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that coupling the in-plane polarity of the Berry curvature ($\mathbf{p}_\Omega$) with a real-space mass gradient ($\mathbf{g}_m$) dictates a geometric selection rule that enables gapless, tunable pseudospin Hall modes.
method: The study combines theoretical modeling of the low-energy Hamiltonian with experimental realization using acoustic resonators to program and verify the geometric selection rule.
model_or_system: The system is based on a pseudospin-1 Dirac Hamiltonian realized in a four-site planar acoustic lattice. The lattice allows independent programming of the Berry-curvature polarity ($\mathbf{p}_\Omega$) via intracell couplings and the spatial mass gradient ($\mathbf{g}_m$) via coupling modulation.
key_observables: Gapless pseudospin Hall modes, directional waveguiding paths, and the pseudospin-momentum locking confirmed by source excitation handedness.
important_parameters: The geometric matching factor $\chi = (\mathbf{p}_\Omega 	imes \mathbf{g}_m) \cdot \hat{z}$, which must equal $+1$ for gapless transport.
main_assumptions: The work establishes a strict geometric selection rule by decoupling the control of $\mathbf{p}_\Omega$ (intracell ratios) from $\mathbf{g}_m$ (real-space arrangement).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the concept of Berry-curvature polarity ($\mathbf{p}_\Omega$) and the resulting spectra based on mass gradient configuration. Subsequent figures detail the four-site lattice structure, showing how couplings control $\mathbf{p}_\Omega$ and $\mathbf{g}_m$, and present experimental acoustic measurements confirming gap closing and directional waveguiding.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the theoretical framework, identifying the Berry-curvature polarity ($\mathbf{p}_\Omega$) and the geometric selection rule involving the mass gradient ($\mathbf{g}_m$). It then details the lattice engineering to independently control these two components. Finally, it presents experimental acoustic measurements confirming the predicted gapless transport and directional control.
why_interesting: The ability to program waveguiding paths by matching momentum-space geometric textures ($\mathbf{p}_\Omega$) with real-space gradients ($\mathbf{g}_m$) offers a general, tunable mechanism for wave manipulation applicable across various physical platforms.
